newsitem.title: INDIA: India police argue in court for Yadav's arrest.
newsitem.headline: India police argue in court for Yadav's arrest.

text.p: India's federal investigation agency argued in a court on Wednesday that it wanted to arrest Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, in a corruption case, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)'s lawyer said in the court in the state capital of Patna that the investigation agency wanted "custodial interrogation" of Yadav in the case linked to a $280 million corruption scandal.
The CBI was arguing against allowing Yadav to be granted "anticipatory bail" allowed under Indian law to people who seek a court's intervention in advance to avoid possible arrest.
Arguments were scheduled to continue on Thursday.
"If the chief minister is allowed to remain free, the ongoing investigations into several cases of the scam will be hampered," PTI quoted lawyer Rakesh Kumar as saying.
Yadav says he is innocent in the case involving alleged siphoning of state animal welfare funds.
Yadav, who recently formed a breakway group of Prime Miister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, has rejected calls from political partners and opposition groups to resign in the case.
Gujral's United Front coalition is badly divided over its continuing association with a breakaway faction, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) set up by Yadav early this month.
